definitions.explanation: The most common verb for verbal expression. Used when someone speaks words or expresses something verbally. Unlike {話|はな}す (hanasu) which emphasizes conversation or storytelling, {言|い}う focuses on the act of uttering specific words or statements.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は「{行|い}きたくない」と{言|い}いました。
examples.english: He said, 'I don't want to go.'

examples.japanese: {本当|ほんとう}のことを{言|い}ってください。

notes: This is a godan verb ending in う. The te-form is {言|い}って. Often used with と to quote speech. Common expressions include {言|い}い{方|かた} (way of saying), {言|い}い{訳|わけ} (excuse), and と{言|い}えば (speaking of).
